Text 961 lines shorter.
notes: Diff of 8,888 lines reviewed by structure: 6 functions changed (61 hunks in each validate function, 4 in each migrated-chain function). After renumbering, the diffs of 9793d84f and 41fe5385 are identical, and 44c3e085 / 0e9d5cb9 differ from them only in the override context and one argument (address(_N) for storK), so 41fe5385 was read in detail (first 820 diff lines line by line, the rest through every changed call, condition and require) and stands for all four. Per validate function the calls (113), reverts (170) and abort (1) are unchanged. Checked by hand: the concat rewrite (lengths _21 + 10, mem[64] = ... + 970, the zero padding word), the two sha3 version comparisons (operand order and bases kept), resourceConfig field checks (uint32(ext_call.return_data[0]) != 20 * 10**6 with no call in between), the stor21 call argument order against the head/tail layout (head 384 / 448 words, offsets 384, 32n + 416, 32n + 128m + 448), and the returned-bytes copy line + 'if ceil32(_64) > _64' padding. Every ext_call.return_data[k] use has no call between it and its call. Minor: uint32(return_data[0]) and return_data[28 len 4] are both used for the same check; one call target prints as address(ext_call.return_data[0]) where the next uses _10 for the same value; '_6 = return_data.size / _10 = ext_call.return_data[0]' are bound before the success check (harmless: both paths revert on short data). Some raw calls remain unfolded where mem[64] comes from a join ('args mem[mem[64] len _1759 - mem[64] + 4]').
summary: One low regression: allocation bases are now inlined as long ceil32 sums (lines over 240 chars 6 -> 72). Big improvement otherwise: 82 calls decoded (including the stor21 migration calls), 90 copy loops removed, P1/P6 gone. The coverage abort and the length-check finding remain; finding 2 is only partly fixed.
